counting.title: How is this counted?
counting.flight: A flight counts once it has taken place – planned and cancelled ones do not. Distance is the great-circle line between the airports.
counting.flightTime: Flight time runs from take-off to landing of the counted flights. A flight with no time is left out and the total reads "at least".
counting.cruise: A cruise counts after its return. Ports count once per port, sea days not; distance follows the sea route.
counting.rail: A journey counts once it is over. Journeys with no known distance are missing from the kilometres, so the total reads "at least".
counting.bus: A ride counts once it is over. Rides with no known distance are missing from the kilometres.
counting.rental: A rental counts after the return; rental days are the days between pick-up and return.
counting.ferry: A crossing counts once it has taken place and belongs to the year it arrived in.
counting.tour: A tour counts once it has happened. If its recording was truncated, the distance is a minimum.
counting.lodging: A stay counts only after check-out – a house you have merely booked is not a visit. Nights are the nights between arrival and departure.
counting.place: A place counts when it is marked as visited; a wishlist place with a future date does not. Visits count only what has already happened.
counting.daysAway: Every calendar day you were away somewhere counts once, even when trips overlap. Only available when all your domains are shared.
counting.countries: Countries from all your trips and places, each once. A lifetime total across all domains only.
counting.curated: Of a standard list's targets, what you ticked as visited counts. Only the number is shared, never which places.
